Plotted against h on a log-log scale (Fig. 13a).); Condition number of the system matrix (Eq. 21) vs mesh size (log10 of the condition number against log10(h) (Fig. 13b).)?

spec.name: Cook's membrane, finite strain: regular-mesh FEM vs tangled-mesh i-TFEM; tip displacement u_y at corner A, H1 error and condition number vs mesh index N
spec.geometry: 2D Cook's membrane (tapered quadrilateral panel). Point A is the top right corner of the right edge. Dimensions are defined in Sec. 4.1 / Fig. 1a, which are not provided. The mesh is a structured 2^N x 2^N family with N = 2 to 6, and the fine-mesh reference is N = 7 (128 x 128). There are three discretisations: regular-mesh FEM, tangled-mesh FEM and tangled-mesh i-TFEM.
spec.material: Not stated in this excerpt. It is presumably hyperelastic (finite strain) and defined in Sec. 4.1/4.2. The neo-Hookean parameters mu=500, K=1700 belong to the punch problem (Sec. 4.3) and must NOT be assumed for Cook's membrane. The compressibility level (K/mu) is unknown, so volumetric locking cannot be assessed.
spec.loading: Incremental finite-strain load stepping, with u_y at A reported at every step (Fig. 10). The load type is assumed to be the standard shear traction on the right edge, but this is not confirmed. The magnitude, number of steps and Newton tolerance are not stated. Boundary conditions are assumed to be the standard ones (left edge clamped, top and bottom edges traction-free, right edge loaded), but the paper's statement is not available.
qois: u_y at corner A vs load step (Fig. 10). This is a global, displacement-type QoI. It should converge under refinement because A is away from the clamped-free corners. It is a usable reference value only if the load level, BCs, material and solver tolerances are known and each load step is converged. Comparing FEM with i-TFEM at a single mesh is a consistency check, not a convergence check.

Maximum vertical displacement in the final deformed configuration (Figs. 11a/b, top of the contour legend). It is NOT trustworthy as a reference: its location is not identified (not stated to be A), the value is read from a colour-legend bound rather than reported, and contour post-processing (nodal extrapolation or smoothing) may affect it. At most, use it as a qualitative cross-check against u_y(A) at the final step.

u_y at A vs mesh index N = 2..6 for regular FEM, tangled FEM and tangled i-TFEM (Fig. 12). This is the best candidate for a trustworthy reference. Use the regular-mesh FEM sequence to check monotone, asymptotic convergence (e.g. Richardson extrapolation or observed order from 3+ consecutive N). Expected: it converges, though possibly with a reduced rate because of the corner singularities. Tangled FEM is expected to be wrong or non-convergent; that is what the paper wants to show and it is not a reference.

H1 seminorm error e_h = ||grad u - grad u_h||_L2 vs h (Eq. 24, Fig. 13a). The 'reference' is the N = 7 discrete solution, not an exact solution, so this is a self-convergence measure. The N = 6 point is only one level from the reference, so its error is underestimated and the apparent rate is biased (usually steepening artificially at the finest level). Exclude the last point or use a reference at least 2 levels finer. The clamped-free corner singularities cap the H1 rate below the smooth-case O(h) for Q4. An observed rate of about 1 or more should be explained, not taken as evidence. Also unclear: how grad u is transferred between the N = 7 mesh and the tangled meshes, and in which configuration the gradient is taken.

Condition number of the system matrix (Eq. 21) vs h (Fig. 13b). This is a solver or stability diagnostic, NOT an accuracy QoI, so it cannot serve as a reference value for the solution. For a regular mesh the expected scaling is about O(h^-2), i.e. a slope of about -2 in log10 vs log10(h). It is a meaningful check of whether i-TFEM restores well-conditioning on tangled meshes. Unknown: which matrix it is (tangent stiffness at which load step, or linearised at the reference configuration?), how it is computed (2-norm, estimate) and whether constrained DOFs are eliminated.
well_posedness: Dirichlet BCs: a clamped left edge (assumed) removes rigid-body modes, so the equilibrium problem is well-posed for each load step if the material is polyconvex or stable. This needs confirmation from Sec. 4.1.

Material stability: the hyperelastic model and parameters are unknown. Ellipticity or polyconvexity at the strains reached must be confirmed. If the material is nearly incompressible (large K/mu), standard Q4 locks and u_y(A) converges slowly or not at all toward the true value.

Load level vs limit points: Cook's membrane under shear loading normally has no limit point at moderate load. However, the load magnitude is not given, so absence of buckling or snap-through and uniqueness of the load-path solution cannot be verified. Each load step must reach Newton convergence for Fig. 10 to be a valid reference.

Singular features: the clamped-edge / traction-free-edge corners (top-left and bottom-left) make pointwise stress and strain singular. Peak stress does not converge, and the H1 error rate is reduced below O(h). The displacement at A, energy and region averages remain convergent. A itself (a free convex corner of the loaded edge) has no singularity in displacement.

Tangled-mesh FEM: elements with inverted or overlapping Jacobians make standard FEM inconsistent, so its results are not a reference. Only regular FEM, and i-TFEM if shown to agree with it, are candidates.
Reference adequacy: N = 7 is only one refinement level beyond the finest test mesh (N = 6). It is adequate for N = 2 to 5 but biases e_h and the convergence assessment at N = 6.
open_questions: Element type and polynomial order (Q4 is assumed only as a placeholder; it could be T3, Q8/Q9 or another type). This decides the expected convergence rates.
Geometry dimensions of Cook's membrane (standard 48/44/16?), defined in Sec. 4.1 / Fig. 1a, which are not provided.
Boundary conditions as stated by the paper (clamped left edge? traction on the right edge? traction-free top and bottom edges?).
Material model and parameters for Cook's membrane (the punch-problem mu=500, K=1700 must not be reused), including the degree of compressibility.
Load type (shear traction vs prescribed displacement), total magnitude, number of load steps and Newton convergence tolerance.
How the N = 7 reference gradient is evaluated against tangled-mesh solutions in Eq. 24 (projection or interpolation operator, quadrature, reference vs current configuration).
Whether the Fig. 11 maximum vertical displacement occurs at A, and its numeric value (only a contour-legend bound is available).
Which matrix is used in the condition number (Eq. 21): the linear stiffness or the tangent at a specified load step; the norm used; and the treatment of Dirichlet DOFs.
Numerical values of u_y(A) for each N and each method (Fig. 12), and e_h values (Fig. 13a). They are only shown graphically, so digitised values would be needed for a deterministic check.
How the tangled meshes are generated, and whether the tangling level is fixed across N (this affects whether the i-TFEM convergence rate is comparable to regular FEM).
